_comment_storage: Structured schema-3 storage declaration. scopes.user 'r' lets the app-side files.download with scope:'user' READ the user-scope objects the bundled Executa wrote (APS rows are always filtered by user_id — this never exposes another user's data). Schema 3 requires the app decl to normalize EQUAL to the bundled Executa's ['aps.files', 'aps.scope.user.read'] — hence files:true (the Executa's files/* surface) and kv:true (legacy aps.scope.* caps imply kv).
system_prompt_addendum: The user has the APS Files Demo app open. It saves text notes to Anna object storage by invoking the bundled files-via-executa Executa (save_note / get_link / list_notes, each accepting scope='user' or scope='tool'). A scope selector demonstrates every APS scope: Executa-side user (user-wide) and tool (plugin-private), plus Host-API-side app. Both modes also demonstrate anna.files.download — the host-mediated browser save where the presigned URL never enters the app iframe (tool mode reads the Executa's scope=user notes via the app's storage.scopes.user read declaration; tool-scope notes are fetched via the Executa's get_link instead). The app itself has no upload grant — all object storage goes through the Executa's aps.files capability.
